summary.headline: GE Power India Q2 FY27 order intake rose 38% YoY to Rs 331 crore, with revenue up 11% to Rs 311 crore and a Rs 561 crore Saudi SHOAIBA award.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 order intake grew 38% YoY to Rs 331 crore, led by core services orders up 43% YoY to Rs 232 crore. Revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 311 crore and H1 revenue reached Rs 620 crore versus Rs 567 crore. Management highlighted the Saudi SHOAIBA fuel conversion award (cumulative Rs 561 crore) and NCLT sanction of the Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy. Reported profit before tax from continuing operations was Rs 553 crore for the quarter versus Rs 46 crore, but the transcript's figures for this line and H1 (Rs 1.2 crore vs Rs 90 crore) are garbled and should be verified against the filed results.

segments.name: Core services
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 orders Rs 232 crore, up 43% YoY; management prioritises short-cycle, higher-margin work with payback of 12-15 months. Core sales rose Rs 40 crore per management.

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: Upgrade sales rose Rs 45 crore per management; upgrades are positioned as the entry point to bring non-GE fleets into the recurring service base. Non-GE fleet is about 15-17% of current order mix.

segments.name: International (SHOAIBA, Saudi Arabia)
segments.commentary: Two notices of award from Dhar Balad in August 2026 with cumulative value of about Rs 561 crore; Rs 76 crore booked in September 2026 and Rs 485 crore expected to be booked in the next quarter. Scope covers equipment supply and field advisory for boiler fuel conversion over 2.5 years, across 12 units.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Demerger to JSW Energy sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai; certified order received 13 Oct 2026. Shareholders get 10 JSW Energy shares for every 139 held. A five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy is in place.

segments.name: Joint venture with NTPC (50%)
segments.commentary: Q2 share of profit is a loss of about Rs 5 crore per an analyst's reading of the consolidated-standalone gap; management said the JV is operationally independent and runs O&M, upgrades and retrofits.

guidance_outlook: Rs 485 crore balance of the SHOAIBA order is expected to be booked in the next quarter (Q3 FY27), based on advance receipt.
Durgapur demerger: remaining regulatory steps pending; record date to be notified to exchanges shortly. Appointed date is 1 April 2025 per management's reference.

Tax: the company is still utilising accumulated losses. Tax on the standalone P&L currently relates only to interest on cash pool lending. Management expects to enter a full tax trajectory in about two years.

Management declined to give revenue or order-book growth targets for two to three years, calling these futuristic. Dividend policy: about Rs 47 crore paid in Sept 2025, described as the highest in 10 years.
capex_capacity: Boiler fuel conversion for SHOAIBA involves refurbishment of existing boilers at 12 units, covering boiler management, fuel management and firing systems. The company supplies engineering, procurement and field advisory; the EPC contractor handles erection and commissioning.
Durgapur facility to move to JSW Energy; JAPEL retains a five-year manufacturing services agreement for fabrication support.
Repair facility expansion at Ahmedabad (Adodra) of about Rs 18 crore, announced September 2025.
Management said the current strategy does not require the Rs 1,000 crore cash pool limit; future investment will be communicated as needed.

CEA plan cited for around 66 GW of refurbishment and for flexible two-shift operation of about 150 units; management said JAPEL is working on five refurbishment units with completion extending to 2028.
demand_pricing: Management cited India electricity generation up 11% YoY to about 536 billion units in Q2 FY27, with thermal plant utilisation rising and demand for availability and life-cycle services.
TAM about Rs 6,500 crore and SAM about Rs 3,700 crore; JAPEL holds about 21% share of SAM.

Receivables of about Rs 750 crore were described as mostly from the legacy FGD/EPC business, with about Rs 350 crore collected from one customer in FY26 under a settlement. Management said current receivables are good and not sticky.
Management did not disclose project-level margins, saying it prefers to report aggregate margins only.
FGD EPC backlog is about 20% of the Rs 1,527 crore backlog, but only about 14-15% of quarterly revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What share of service orders and revenue comes from third-party (non-GE) fleets, and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-GE fleet is about 15-17% of the current order mix. Management declined to give a three-year target, calling it futuristic. Upgrades on non-GE units are the route to bring them into the recurring service base.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the Rs 741 crore cash pool lending deployed, and on what terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Lent to the GE Vernova group cash pool header (Privaly Ltd, a GE Vernova subsidiary) at 5.65-6.25%, repayable on demand and backed by a parent corporate guarantee from GE Vernova. The Rs 1,000 crore limit was approved at the August 2026 AGM. Management said this does not mean Rs 1,000 crore of surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: When will the order book reach four digits, given the CEA refurbishment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is market-driven and that it has a strong track record on the RSQ (refurbishment) work. It is working on five units, with completion extending to 2028; no year-specific timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the NTPC JV work, and does the company control its direction?
qa_highlights.answer: The 50:50 JV is a separate legal entity with its own board and does O&M, upgrades, retrofits and now owner's engineering. It is governed by the promoter agreement but takes its own decisions. The Rs 5 crore loss in the quarter came from the JV, not the 100% boiler services subsidiary, which management said is not operating.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Durgapur demerger remove losses from the continuing business after it becomes effective?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Durgapur profits and losses are in discontinued operations and will move out with the demerger, with effect from the appointed date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and lumpiness outlook, and what does the SHOAIBA project involve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the SHOAIBA job is a refurbishment of existing boilers, with EPC contractors handling erection. It declined to give project margins individually and said the overall strategy is high-margin, short-cycle work.

risks_watch: Revenue growth is 11% YoY and H1 revenue growth is about 9%, while profit lines are unclear in the transcript; verify PBT figures against the filed results.
Execution of the Rs 485 crore SHOAIBA balance and the Rs 76 crore booked in September, given advance-based timing and a 2.5-year window.
Durgapur demerger completion: regulatory steps remaining and the record date.
Receivables of about Rs 750 crore, mostly legacy FGD/EPC; monitor collection and any reduction.
Related-party exposure: Rs 741 crore cash pool lending to the GE Vernova group entity at 5.65-6.25%, repayable on demand.
Lumpy quarterly numbers; management did not address smoothing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order momentum, the SHOAIBA win and the NCLT approval, but evasive on forward targets (non-GE share, revenue growth, order book four-digit timing, project margins). Answers on the cash pool and the JV were specific and factual.
key_quotes: We have successfully shifted our focus from volume-driven revenue, changing to prioritization of higher-margin, shorter-cycle, cash-accretive opportunities.
The trade receivables which you see as on 30 September, 26, are all good and there is nothing sticky or I would say and thoughtful in this.
So it's not a re-installation from the start or something like that for a new erection.
We have actually decided to not to go for the long EPC gestation projects. We want to go for the projects which are short cycles.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management declined to give growth targets for 2-3 years. Q2 order intake up 38% (core services orders up 43%) and the Rs 561 crore SHOAIBA award (Rs 485 crore to be booked in Q3 FY27) back near-term growth, while Rs 18 crore Adodra repair expansion is the only capacity addition cited.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says the strategy favours high-margin, short-cycle core services with 12-15 month paybacks, but it declined to disclose project margins, and the Rs 5 crore JV loss and unclear PBT figures cloud the trend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only capacity addition cited is the Rs 18 crore Adodra repair facility expansion announced Sept 2025 with no size or completion date given, and utilisation was not disclosed, so no major new capacity is firmly committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 order intake rose 38% YoY to Rs 331 crore and Rs 485 crore of SHOAIBA is expected to be booked in Q3 FY27, against Rs 1,527 crore backlog, while India generation rose 11% YoY to about 536 BU.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said the current strategy does not need the Rs 1,000 crore cash pool limit and no utilisation level was disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement in the window looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 order intake rose 38% YoY to Rs 331 crore (core services up 43%) and the Rs 561 crore SHOAIBA award is building the order book, but management gave no numeric guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The Rs 485 crore SHOAIBA balance is advance-dependent and due in Q3 FY27, and H1 revenue growth was only about 9% (Rs 620 crore vs Rs 567 crore), so slippage risk exists, though no formal guidance was given.

rows.label: SHOAIBA Saudi boiler fuel conversion award
rows.why: Rs 561 crore cumulative award with Rs 76 crore booked in September 2026 and Rs 485 crore expected to be booked in the next quarter based on advance receipt.

rows.label: Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy
rows.why: NCLT Mumbai sanctioned the demerger and the certified order was received 13 Oct 2026, with shareholders getting 10 JSW shares per 139 held, but record date and remaining regulatory steps are pending.

rows.label: Receivables collection from legacy FGD/EPC
rows.why: About Rs 750 crore of receivables are mostly legacy FGD/EPC, with about Rs 350 crore collected from one customer in FY26 under a settlement, and management says current receivables are good and not sticky.

tone.note: Management was confident on order momentum, the SHOAIBA award and NCLT approval but evasive on forward targets such as non-GE share, growth, four-digit order book timing and project margins; analysts probed the cash pool, the JV loss and the margin outlook.

quality.why: Revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 311 crore (Rs 281 crore base) with management attributing growth to core sales (+Rs 40 crore) and upgrades (+Rs 45 crore), which looks volume-led, but the brief gives no volume percentage and profit lines are garbled so the earnings quality cannot be confirmed; the Rs 76 crore SHOAIBA booking is order intake, not revenue, and no one-offs are quantified in the brief.
